title: Le Chatelier's Principle (numericals not required)
notes: Le Chatelier's principle: if a system at equilibrium is disturbed by a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that tends to oppose that change.
Adding a reactant, or removing a product, shifts the equilibrium toward the products. Adding a product, or removing a reactant, shifts it toward the reactants.

Raising the pressure shifts a gas equilibrium toward the side with fewer moles of gas. Lowering the pressure shifts it toward the side with more moles of gas. If both sides have the same number of gas moles, a pressure change does not move the position.

For an exothermic forward reaction, raising the temperature shifts the equilibrium toward the reactants, the endothermic direction. Lowering the temperature shifts it toward the products. A catalyst speeds both directions equally and does not change the equilibrium position.
This topic asks for the direction of the shift. It does not ask for a new numerical value of the equilibrium constant.
